notes.tone: A drinking party that has argued itself into a question. Socrates is enjoying it, Leonidas is enduring it, Medusa is bored by it, the Cyclops has not followed it. The comedy is legends treating their own legends as ordinary.
notes.difficulty: Second table. The contempt is sharper than at the White House: the player is not a guest here, they are an exhibit. It turns when the table starts arguing WITH the player instead of ABOUT them.
notes.dealer_plant: The single 'the dealer arranged it' beat is at_plant_01 to at_plant_04. Do NOT add a second. It is also the only question Socrates ever declines to ask.
notes.nickname: Tier 1 is 'Nobody' — the false name Odysseus gave Polyphemus (Odyssey 9). It is the symposium's word for its test case, it is a running sore for the Cyclops, and Nobody -> {name} -> Hero is the answer to the table's question.
notes.odysseus: Arrives about 10 hands after the first elimination (tables/athens.json). Every line with speaker 'odysseus', and the cyclops_odysseus banter, fires only once he is seated. If the player clears the table first, champion_missed plays INSTEAD of champion_arrival / champion_headsup / champion_defeat's first line; Death's count line at_od_end_02 still closes the table.
notes.medusa: Her tells are inverted in the data. No line explains this. Lines may hint that watching her face teaches the wrong lesson; none may say so outright.
notes.cyclops_eye: Homer's Polyphemus is blinded by Odysseus. At this table the eye is scarred but works, and no line draws attention to it. He recognises Odysseus by VOICE on purpose, which reads correctly either way.
notes.gods: Gods are reserved for the sequel. They are only ever mentioned in passing ('my father', 'the sea-god', Ovid's Neptune and Minerva). None appears or speaks.
notes.leak_rule: No line may reference hand strength while cards are live.
notes.voice: Champion (Odysseus) + Death are voiced. Socrates / Leonidas / Medusa / the Cyclops are text + vocalization for now.
notes.sources: Homer (Odyssey 9, 11, 12, 17), Plato (Symposium, Apology, Phaedo), Herodotus (6.106, 6.120, 7.220), Plutarch (Sayings of Spartans), Hesiod (Theogony), Ovid (Metamorphoses 4). Nothing from the film 300.

respect_tiers.0: Contempt. The player is the question under discussion, not a person anyone speaks to.
respect_tiers.1: Grudging notice. Socrates names the test case 'Nobody'. The Cyclops objects.
respect_tiers.2: Real address. They argue WITH the player now, not about them.
respect_tiers.3: Title. Earned. The question is answered: Hero. Socrates says it first — he asked the question.

table_intro.speaker: death
table_intro.text: A symposium. Couches, lamps, a bowl of wine and water, and an argument that has been going since dusk.

table_intro.speaker: death
table_intro.text: They asked for the best dealer. I was available.
table_intro.foreshadow: Reads as dry self-regard. He is the dealer every mortal gets in the end, and he is always available.

table_intro.speaker: death
table_intro.text: The question is whether a mortal nobody can be worth anything. They needed a nobody. Take the chair.

dealer_plant.speaker: leonidas
dealer_plant.text: And you did not ask him why? You ask everyone why.

dealer_plant.speaker: socrates
dealer_plant.text: [glances at the dealer, then back to his cup, and lets it go]
dealer_plant.note: THE SHRUG. The one man who questions everything does not question the dealer. The player never gets an answer.

socrates_leonidas.relationship: Athens against Sparta: talk against silence, and a long rivalry. Herodotus says the Spartans reached Marathon only after the battle, having waited for the full moon, and then went to look at the Persian dead and praised the Athenians. Plato has Socrates praise Sparta's laws, which a Spartan would find more suspicious than an insult.

exchanges.speaker: socrates
exchanges.text: Tell me, King. When the Persians landed at Marathon, where was Sparta?

exchanges.speaker: leonidas
exchanges.text: Waiting for the full moon.

exchanges.speaker: socrates
exchanges.text: And did the Persians wait for it too?

exchanges.speaker: leonidas
exchanges.text: We came afterwards. We said well done. Once.

exchanges.speaker: leonidas
exchanges.text: You have drunk every cup they poured you.

exchanges.speaker: socrates
exchanges.text: And have I once seemed drunk to you?

exchanges.speaker: leonidas
exchanges.text: No. That is what I dislike about you.

exchanges.speaker: socrates
exchanges.text: You answer every question in a single word, King. Is that because the answer is simple, or because the question is?

exchanges.speaker: leonidas
exchanges.text: Yes.

cyclops_odysseus.relationship: Odyssey, Book 9. Odysseus walked into the Cyclops's cave, got him drunk, told him his name was Nobody, blinded him, and escaped clinging under his favourite ram — then shouted his real name from the boat. Polyphemus prayed to his father Poseidon, which is why the voyage home took ten years. Fires only once Odysseus is seated.

exchanges.speaker: cyclops
exchanges.text: You. Little man. Say your name.

exchanges.speaker: odysseus
exchanges.text: Nobody.

exchanges.speaker: cyclops
exchanges.text: [the table groans as he half rises]

exchanges.speaker: odysseus
exchanges.text: A joke! It's Odysseus. I did tell you. From the boat.

exchanges.speaker: cyclops
exchanges.text: I told my father what you did.

exchanges.speaker: odysseus
exchanges.text: Yes. I noticed. For ten years, I noticed.

exchanges.speaker: cyclops
exchanges.text: A seer told me a man would take my eye. I watched for a big one. Handsome. Strong.

exchanges.speaker: odysseus
exchanges.text: Well. Two out of three.

exchanges.speaker: cyclops
exchanges.text: Which two?

socrates_cyclops.relationship: The man of the marketplace and the giant with no marketplace: Homer says the Cyclopes hold no assemblies and have no laws. And when the oracle at Delphi was asked whether anyone was wiser than Socrates, it answered that no one was — which is the wrong way to put it in front of Polyphemus.

exchanges.speaker: socrates
exchanges.text: Someone once asked the oracle at Delphi who was wiser than me. The answer was: nobody.

exchanges.speaker: cyclops
exchanges.text: Do not say that word.

exchanges.speaker: socrates
exchanges.text: Which word? 'Wiser'?

exchanges.speaker: socrates
exchanges.text: Tell me, how do the Cyclopes make their laws?

exchanges.speaker: cyclops
exchanges.text: No laws. Each one rules his own cave.

exchanges.speaker: socrates
exchanges.text: And if two of you want the same sheep?

exchanges.speaker: cyclops
exchanges.text: Then there is one Cyclops.

leonidas_medusa.relationship: The man who is not afraid of anything, and the face that was made to cause fear — Greek soldiers painted it on their shields. Also, as Herodotus records, Leonidas's wife was named Gorgo.

exchanges.speaker: medusa
exchanges.text: You are looking straight at me, Spartan.

exchanges.speaker: leonidas
exchanges.text: Spartans do not look away.

exchanges.speaker: medusa
exchanges.text: No. In my experience, they stop looking all at once.

exchanges.speaker: leonidas
exchanges.text: My wife's name is Gorgo.

exchanges.speaker: medusa
exchanges.text: Is it. And is she frightening?

exchanges.speaker: leonidas
exchanges.text: She is Spartan.

tier_0.speaker: socrates
tier_0.text: So this is what we have been arguing about all night. It is smaller than I pictured.

tier_0.speaker: leonidas
tier_0.text: In Sparta the elders look at every newborn. They would have had questions about you.

tier_0.speaker: cyclops
tier_0.text: Small. Soft. I have eaten bigger guests than this.

tier_0.speaker: medusa
tier_0.text: Go on, look at me. Everyone does, once.

tier_1.speaker: socrates
tier_1.text: Well. You are not nothing, it seems. Then let us call you Nobody, and see what Nobody can do.
tier_1.note: The announcement. Speaks the nickname literally.

tier_1.speaker: cyclops
tier_1.text: Nobody. Of all the names. I hate that name.
tier_1.note: Odysseus told him his name was Nobody before blinding him (Odyssey 9).

tier_1.speaker: leonidas
tier_1.text: You stood when you were pushed. Barely. It is more than most Athenians manage.

tier_1.speaker: medusa
tier_1.text: You looked away at the right moment. Most people learn that too late.

tier_2.speaker: socrates
tier_2.text: {name}. I withdraw 'Nobody'. The evidence no longer supports it.
tier_2.note: First use of the player's real name. Socrates named the test case, so he retires the name.

tier_2.speaker: medusa
tier_2.text: You don't flinch from me any more. Or stare. Either one would have been a mistake.

tier_2.speaker: cyclops
tier_2.text: You are small. But you are not soft.

tier_2.speaker: odysseus
tier_2.text: I was Nobody once myself. It's an excellent place to start from.

tier_3.speaker: socrates
tier_3.text: Hero. The question is settled, and against me. I have always enjoyed being refuted.
tier_3.note: Socrates gives the title because he asked the question. If he is already out, at_p3_04 (Odysseus) also opens with the title and can carry the announcement. Plato's Socrates says he would rather be refuted than refute (Gorgias).

tier_3.speaker: leonidas
tier_3.text: In Sparta, praise is one word. Good.

tier_3.speaker: medusa
tier_3.text: Perseus had a mirror, and help. You had neither.

tier_3.speaker: odysseus
tier_3.text: Hero. Careful. The next thing they do is send you somewhere far away for twenty years.

death_asides.speaker: death
death_asides.text: Take your time. At Potidaea, Socrates stood thinking from one dawn to the next. Soldiers brought their bedding out to watch.

death_asides.speaker: death
death_asides.text: The Greeks would blame three sisters with a thread. I only shuffled.

death_asides.speaker: death
death_asides.text: Twenty years getting home. He can stand to lose a pot.

death_asides.speaker: death
death_asides.text: One chair empty. Someone has been expected for some time.
death_asides.note: Starts the clock on Odysseus's arrival.

death_asides.speaker: death
death_asides.text: In Athens they voted people out with broken pottery. You have found a quicker way.

death_asides.speaker: death
death_asides.text: All of it. The Greeks had a word for this. Two, depending on how it goes.

death_asides.speaker: death
death_asides.text: Two left. They always think this is the last table.
death_asides.foreshadow: Reads as poker talk, or fatalism about mortals. The last table is his, and they are always wrong about which one it is.

champion_arrival.speaker: narration
champion_arrival.text: The street door opens on a gust of salt air. A weathered man stands in it, dripping on the floor, and counts the exits before he counts the guests.

champion_arrival.speaker: odysseus
champion_arrival.text: Forgive me. I was held up. There was a whirlpool, and then an island, and the island took seven years.

champion_arrival.speaker: cyclops
champion_arrival.note: The grudge payoff. If the Cyclops is already out, end the sequence at at_arr_02.

champion_arrival.speaker: odysseus
champion_arrival.text: Do you? I have one of those voices.

champion_missed.speaker: narration
champion_missed.text: The street door opens on a gust of salt air. A weathered man stands in it, dripping, and looks at an empty table.

champion_missed.speaker: odysseus
champion_missed.text: Over? Already? I was told dusk. Nobody said which dusk.

champion_missed.speaker: odysseus
champion_missed.text: Well. Next time save me a chair, and don't win quite so quickly.
champion_missed.note: Mildly put out, not angry. The visible cost of the skip: he is greyed out in the ledger until the table is replayed. Death's count line at_od_end_02 follows.

champion_headsup.speaker: odysseus
champion_headsup.text: Just the two of us. Good. I've talked my way out of worse rooms with fewer friends.

champion_headsup.speaker: odysseus
champion_headsup.text: I came home dressed as a beggar once. The only one who knew me on sight was the dog.

champion_headsup.speaker: odysseus
champion_headsup.text: I had myself tied to a mast once, to hear a song and not die of it. This is easier. Slightly.

champion_headsup.speaker: odysseus
champion_headsup.text: Oh, well done. Truly. I'd have tried that myself.

socrates.speaker: socrates
socrates.text: Out. Good — now I can ask questions without anyone suspecting a motive.

socrates.speaker: socrates
socrates.text: I have left gatherings in worse circumstances. Someone remember that I owe a rooster.
socrates.note: His last words in the Phaedo: a debt of a cockerel to Asclepius.

leonidas.speaker: leonidas
leonidas.text: [takes up his helmet and goes without a word]

medusa.speaker: medusa
medusa.text: Don't watch me go. It never ends well for anyone who does.

medusa.speaker: medusa
medusa.text: Well. At least this time I keep my head.

cyclops.speaker: cyclops
cyclops.note: What he shouted to the other Cyclopes, who went home (Odyssey 9).

cyclops.speaker: cyclops
cyclops.text: I go back to my sheep. Sheep do not cheat.

odysseus.speaker: odysseus
odysseus.text: Well. I've been shipwrecked before. I'll wash up somewhere.

odysseus.speaker: odysseus
odysseus.text: I'm going home. It may take a while.

player_busted.speaker: death
player_busted.text: Sit a while. The argument is not over, and they will want their test case back.

player_busted.speaker: socrates
player_busted.text: Don't be downcast. One result is not a proof. Come back, and we will examine it again.

player_busted.speaker: leonidas
player_busted.text: You fell facing forward. That counts.

champion_defeat.speaker: odysseus
champion_defeat.text: Well played. I've lost twelve ships in my time. I can lose a table.

champion_defeat.speaker: death
champion_defeat.text: Two. Six remain. Take the long way round, if you like. Everyone arrives in the end.
champion_defeat.foreshadow: Sounds like a nod to Odysseus's voyage. Everyone does arrive in the end — at him.
champion_defeat.note: Also closes the table after champion_missed.
